title: Org owner adds a payment method via Stripe-hosted Checkout (setup mode), then the checkout.session.completed webhook records it
description: There is no embedded Stripe Elements/card form anywhere in the client — 'add card' is a full-page redirect to a Stripe Checkout Session created in mode:'setup'. Verifies the real end-to-end path, not a fabricated in-app card form. Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — Stripe Checkout, checkout-session, and the 'Set up payment' CTA were deleted entirely; there is no payment-method setup flow of any kind in the current codebase.
preconditions: Org has no stripeCustomerId yet; plan.status='pending_payment'
steps: Navigate to /billing-plans Overview tab and confirm the 'Set up payment' CTA is shown
Click the CTA, which calls billingService.startCheckoutSetup() -> POST /billing/v1/billing/checkout-session
Follow the redirect to the returned Stripe session.url and complete card entry on the Stripe-hosted page
Confirm Stripe redirects back to {CLIENT_APP_URL}/billing?setup=success
Wait for the checkout.session.completed webhook to be processed
expectedResult: Org's billing.stripeCustomerId is now set, the 'Set up payment' CTA no longer appears on Overview, and any frameworks previously pending payment are activated.

title: Selecting a higher tier on the Plans tab upgrades the plan and updates Overview without a full page reload
preconditions: Org on 'growth' tier with a payment method already on file
steps: Navigate to /billing-plans, open the Plans tab
Select the 'scale' plan and confirm via UpgradeModal
Observe the POST /billing/v1/billing/plan/upgrade call and its 200 response
Switch to the Overview tab without reloading the browser
expectedResult: Overview now shows tier 'scale', updated moduleConfig limits/usage bars, and no 'requires_contact' prompt since this tier is self-serve.
description: Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — selecting a plan on the Plans tab no longer upgrades anything directly; it submits a SubscriptionRequest that requires admin/MSSP approval before any entitlement changes. See BILL-E2E-009.

title: Downgrade is scheduled for the next renewal date, plan access is unchanged until then, and the scheduled change can be cancelled
description: Downgrades are never immediate — they are stored as a pending-tier-change applied at renewsAt. PendingDowngradeBanner surfaces the scheduled date and a Cancel action. Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — the pending-tier-change document and PendingDowngradeBanner's data source (plan.pendingChange) no longer exist; subscription.controller.js's getCurrent() never populates pendingChange, so the banner is now dead code. See BILL-E2E-012 and BILL-SAN-007.
preconditions: Org on 'scale' tier, usage within 'growth' tier limits
steps: On the Plans tab, choose to downgrade to 'growth'
Confirm via DowngradeModal (no over-cap dialog expected since usage is within limits)
Reload /billing-plans and check the Overview tab for PendingDowngradeBanner
Verify a scale-tier-only feature (behind TierGate) is still fully accessible, not degraded
Click 'Cancel' on PendingDowngradeBanner
expectedResult: Banner reads 'scheduled to downgrade to growth on <renewsAt date>'. Scale-tier features remain accessible while the downgrade is pending. After clicking Cancel, DELETE /billing/v1/billing/plan/pending-change succeeds and the banner disappears with the org remaining on 'scale' tier indefinitely.

title: A TierGate-wrapped premium feature shows the upgrade alert on a lower tier and unlocks after a real upgrade
description: TierGate.jsx is now a thin wrapper checking entitlements?.entitlementValues?.[feature]===true, with a generic 'Feature not included' alert (no longer naming the required tier — see BILL-SAN-006). Real enforcement is the backend requireEntitlement middleware, returning errorCode ENTITLEMENT_NOT_AVAILABLE. This case verifies the two still agree end-to-end, since a UI-only gate with no backend check would be a security gap. Note: since plan changes are no longer instant, 'a real upgrade' now means an admin/MSSP-approved SubscriptionRequest, not an immediate self-serve action.
preconditions: Org's entitlements lack a boolean-gated feature (e.g. 'module.vciso.enabled' is not true)
steps: Navigate to a page/section gated behind TierGate for that entitlement key
Observe the Alert: 'Feature not included' / 'This feature is not included in your current plan.' with a 'View plans' button
Attempt to call the underlying API route directly (bypassing the UI) while still lacking the entitlement
Have an admin/MSSP approve a SubscriptionRequest that grants the entitlement, then revisit the same page
expectedResult: Direct API call is rejected 403 { errorCode:'ENTITLEMENT_NOT_AVAILABLE' } even though the button is merely hidden client-side (confirms server-side parity, not just a UI label). After the request is approved and applied, the page renders the actual feature content instead of the gate alert.

title: Invoice history lists Stripe invoices with correctly formatted amount/date, and PDF is obtained via Stripe's hosted invoice page
description: There is no backend PDF proxy/download endpoint — the app only stores and links to Stripe's hosted_invoice_url, which itself offers a PDF download on Stripe's own page. Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — there is no invoice history feature, Stripe hosted invoice page, or PDF download path anywhere in the current codebase.
preconditions: Org has at least 2 historical Stripe invoices with different amounts and currencies formatting
steps: Navigate to the invoice history page (/billing/invoices)
Verify each row's amount matches the Stripe invoice's amount_due, formatted as currency
Verify issuedAt is formatted as a readable date, not a raw epoch/ISO string
Click a row to open its hostedInvoiceUrl
On the Stripe-hosted page, download the PDF
expectedResult: Amounts and dates render correctly and match the Stripe dashboard for the same invoices. The PDF download happens entirely on Stripe's hosted page; there is no in-app 'Download PDF' button that produces a locally-generated file.

title: Full-account cancellation (customer.subscription.deleted) revokes access immediately with no grace period
description: Unlike framework-level cancellation, a whole-org Stripe subscription deletion sets Organization.subscription.status and SubscriptionOrg.status to 'cancelled' immediately — there is no org-level grace window. Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — there is no Stripe subscription or customer.subscription.deleted webhook; full-account cancellation is now a SubscriptionRequest of type cancel_subscription or the admin-only POST /api/admin/billing/clients/:orgId/cancel endpoint.
preconditions: Org has an active org-level Stripe subscription
steps: Cancel the org's Stripe subscription (via Stripe dashboard/test mode) so a customer.subscription.deleted event fires
Wait for the webhook to be processed
Log in as an org user and attempt to access any paid-tier feature
expectedResult: Both Organization.subscription.status and SubscriptionOrg.status read 'cancelled' immediately after the webhook, and paid-tier features are inaccessible with no grace period grant.

title: Cancelling a single framework's subscription enters a 90-day grace period and revokes the framework license immediately
description: Framework-scoped cancellation is handled differently from full-account cancellation: frameworkSubscriptions.$.status becomes 'grace' with graceEndsAt = now + 90 days, while ClientFramework.status is set to 'license_revoked' right away — i.e. the license is revoked immediately even though billing calls it a 'grace period'. Worth confirming this naming doesn't mislead users into thinking they retain framework access during the 90 days. Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — framework-level Stripe subscriptions and the 90-day grace/license_revoked webhook flow no longer exist; framework add/remove is now a SubscriptionRequest of type framework with no grace-period concept found in the current code.
preconditions: Org has 2+ frameworks each with their own framework-level Stripe subscription
steps: Cancel only one framework's Stripe subscription so a framework-scoped customer.subscription.deleted event fires
Wait for the webhook to be processed
Check the framework's subscription status and graceEndsAt, and the ClientFramework.status
As an org user, attempt to access that framework's compliance map
expectedResult: frameworkSubscriptions status='grace' with graceEndsAt ~90 days out, but ClientFramework.status='license_revoked' immediately, and the framework's compliance map/features are inaccessible right away (grace period does not extend feature access, only likely data-retention/reactivation window).

title: Overview tab's 'Renews In N Days' stat is the only renewal/trial countdown surfaced — there is no dedicated trial-ending banner
description: No trial countdown banner component exists anywhere in vibrantix-client-panel. The closest analog is BillingOverview.jsx's generic 'Renews In N Days' stat card, now computed from subscription.controller.js getCurrent()'s plan.renewsAt (sourced from resolved.instance.termEnd), shown for any plan status, not specifically flagged during a trial or when trial-ending is imminent. plan.trialExpiresAt is populated only when resolved.instance.status==='trial', but no UI consumes it separately from the renewal stat.
preconditions: Org's SubscriptionInstance has status='trial' with termEnd 2 days out
steps: Navigate to /billing-plans Overview tab
Locate the 'Renews In N Days' stat card
Confirm no separate persistent trial-ending warning banner is present anywhere in the app shell (top nav, dashboard, or billing pages)
expectedResult: Current behavior: only the generic 'Renews In N Days' stat reflects the approaching trialExpiresAt; there is no visually distinct 'trial ending soon' banner or in-app countdown beyond this stat card. Document as a gap versus the commonly expected trial-countdown-banner UX rather than a defect against a feature that was implemented differently.

title: End-to-end: customer submits a plan-change request, an admin approves it in vibrantix-admin-panel, and the customer's Overview/Usage reflects the new plan — with no payment step anywhere
preconditions: Org on a lower-tier plan with no active MSSP relationship
An admin-panel user with admin:billing:enterprise scope
steps: As the org's billing.update user, open the client-panel Subscription Requests tab and submit a 'Plan upgrade or switch' request
Confirm the toast names the correct reviewer ('the platform administrator')
As the admin, open vibrantix-admin-panel's subscription requests queue and approve the request
Back in the client panel, reload the Overview/Usage tabs
expectedResult: The request shows status 'applied' in Request History with an appliedAt timestamp. Overview now reflects the new plan's label/limits, and Usage's entitlement balances reflect the new plan's limitValue — all without any Stripe/payment-method step at any point in the flow.

title: An AI-metered action that would exceed the remaining ai.credits balance triggers the credit-shortage UI, and requesting a credit pack replenishes the balance once approved
description: Exercises the reserve/QuotaExceededError path end-to-end from a real AI feature (e.g. Smart Compliance run, which spends smart_compliance.ai_credits_per_run against 'ai.credits') through to CreditPackModal's add-on request flow.
preconditions: Org's 'ai.credits' balance has just enough remaining to be exceeded by one more AI action
steps: Trigger an AI-metered action that would push ai.credits usage over its limit
Confirm the caller surfaces a quota-exceeded state to the user (TopUpModal or equivalent)
Open CreditPackModal and request an AI credit pack (e.g. 'AI Silver')
As an admin, approve the resulting add_on SubscriptionRequest
Retry the original AI-metered action
expectedResult: The initial AI action is blocked with a user-facing quota message rather than a raw 402. After the credit pack request is approved, the org's EntitlementBalance for 'ai.credits' increases by the pack's granted amount (e.g. 1200 for ai_silver), and the retried AI action now succeeds.

title: AI Credits History tab lists commit-only usage events with correct service labels and paginates beyond 25 rows
preconditions: Org has more than 25 'ai.credits' commit-operation EntitlementUsageEvent rows across at least 2 different sourceService values (e.g. 'b:smart-compliance' and 'assistant-service:chat')
steps: Open the AI Credits History tab (AiCreditsHistory.jsx)
Verify the Service column shows the human label from AI_CREDIT_SOURCE_LABELS (e.g. 'Smart Compliance', 'AI Assistant') rather than the raw sourceService string
Verify 'reserve' and 'cancel' operations never appear as rows — only 'commit'
Paginate to page 2 and confirm rows/order continue correctly by occurredAt descending
expectedResult: Only commit-operation events are shown, each with a human-readable service label; unmapped sourceService values fall back to the raw string. Pagination metadata (page/limit/total/pages) matches the actual row count, and page 2 shows the next 25 most-recent events with no duplicates or gaps versus page 1.

title: After submitting a downgrade request, entitlements remain fully accessible and the only visible indication is the Request History table — PendingDowngradeBanner never renders
description: Confirms a real (not assumed) UI gap: subscription.controller.js's getCurrent() plan object has no pendingChange field, so PendingDowngradeBanner.jsx's `if (!pendingChange...) return null` guard means it can never render post-rewrite, even though it is still mounted in BillingPlans.jsx.
preconditions: Org submits a 'downgrade' SubscriptionRequest with effectivePolicy='term_end'
steps: Submit the downgrade request via DowngradeModal
Reload /billing-plans and check the Plans tab for any pending-downgrade banner
Check the Subscription Requests history table for the same request
Attempt to access a feature only available on the current (higher) tier
expectedResult: No pending-downgrade banner appears anywhere on the page (confirmed dead code, not a missed manual check). The Subscription Requests history table is the only place the pending downgrade is visible, showing status 'submitted'/'approved' and the target effective date. The higher-tier feature remains fully accessible, since entitlements are unchanged until the request is actually applied at term end.
